name: Pseudopolynomial and modular subset-sum structure results (dense end of the dichotomy)
description: Cluster of results for the dense/pseudopolynomial end of subset sum: a deterministic O(m)-time algorithm for modular subset sum (Le and Le, arXiv 2609.30992), Chan's first deterministic O~(t) all-targets algorithm (arXiv 2601.01390, also derandomizing the output-sensitive algorithms of Bringmann-Nakos and Bringmann-Fischer-Nakos), and the Bringmann-Wellnitz dense subset sum dichotomy (arXiv 2010.09096). They show that when the modulus, target or output size is polynomial in n, subset sum is (near-)linear time. They say nothing about the exponential regime with 2^{Omega(n)} distinct sums, which is where C1/C2 live.
authors_year_venue: Le and Le, arXiv 2609.30992 (Sept 2026); T. M. Chan, arXiv 2601.01390 (Jan 2026); Bringmann and Wellnitz, SODA 2021, arXiv 2010.09096; Bringmann-Fischer-Nakos 'Beating Bellman's algorithm for subset sum', SODA 2025 (not read directly, described via Chan's paper).
status_and_verification: Full text of 2609.30992 and 2601.01390 retrieved and read via alphaXiv (all sections, proofs skimmed). Bringmann-Wellnitz: abstract only (web search), proofs not read. Bringmann-Fischer-Nakos: known only through Chan's description of it (Section 3) and citations; primary text not read. 2609.30992 is a very recent preprint (v2, 29 Sep 2026), not peer reviewed; Chan 2601.01390 is a preprint, venue not checked.
key_theorem_or_bound: Le-Le Thm 1.1: for every m>=1, exact modular subset sum on compact input (<=m records (x,c_x)) is solved deterministically in O(m) time and O(m) auxiliary words, returning all reachable residues and a witness using <= m-1 copies; Cor 1.2: explicit list of n residues in O(n+m). Chan Thm 2.7: all-targets subset sum Sigma(X) ∩ [t] deterministically in O~(t); Thm 3.10: O~(|OUT| sqrt(n)); Thm 3.11: O~(|OUT|^{4/3}) deterministic. Chan quotes the ABHS SETH bound: no O(t^{1-eps} 2^{o(n)}). Bringmann-Wellnitz: near-linear O~(n) iff t >> max_X * Sigma_X / n^2 (up to the stated conditional lower bound under SETH + Strong k-SUM); multiset version has non-matching bounds.
regime_exponents: All results are in the polynomial regime: time poly(n) when m, t, max(X) or |OUT| are poly(n). In the C1/C2 language this is the 'every subset sum value is hit by 2^{n-O(log n)} subsets' extreme, i.e. bin size beta close to 2^n, far above the AKKN threshold 2^{0.661n}. The |OUT|-sensitive algorithms beat 2^{n/2} when |OUT|^{4/3} < 2^{n/2} (|OUT| < 2^{0.375n}) or |OUT| sqrt(n) < 2^{n/2} (|OUT| < 2^{n/2}/sqrt(n)); equivalently the number D=|OUT| of distinct subset sums controls cost. Nothing is known here for 0.311n-style thresholds on D*, which concerns balanced half-sums of a solution support rather than total distinct sums. [uncertain] the exact translation between |OUT|-sensitive thresholds and beta thresholds was derived by me, not stated in the sources.
proof_type_and_tools: Le-Le: combinatorial/algorithmic (runs of reachable residues along cycles of repeated addition, prime-ordered subgroup chain, gcd classes, radix sort); the only additive-combinatorics input is DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar-Samal: a set of >= 8 sqrt(L) distinct units in Z_L has all subset sums Z_L, bounding adaptive sorting batches by O(m^{3/4}). Chan: discrepancy/halver construction via canonical subsets from Koiliaris-Xu dyadic divide and conquer, method of conditional expectation (Chazelle); output-sensitive version uses sumset sparse convolution and Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa submultiplicativity |A1+...+Ar| <= |Sigma|^{1+1/(r-1)}. Bringmann-Wellnitz: Galil-Margalit style additive combinatorics.
quantitative_loss: Le-Le: no loss, exact O(m). Chan: polylog factors in t (probably below 20 log factors, per the paper's remark); halver additive error O~(k/sqrt(b)) is sublinear in k, so recursion survives. The output-sensitive derandomization loses polylogs in n,t rather than in |OUT|. None of these quantities is exponential-energy-sensitive: they all pay at least |OUT|, so with exponential energy / exponentially many sums they give no saving below 2^{n/2} unless |OUT| < 2^{n/2}.
worst_case_vs_average_case: All are deterministic worst-case guarantees, but the guarantee is parameterized (modulus m, target t, or output size), so they transfer to worst-case {0,1} subset sum only on the sub-family where the parameter is small. No average-case content.
coefficient_set: Subset sums with {0,1} coefficients (each copy used at most once); multisets/multiplicities supported (Le-Le compact input with counts c_x; Chan remarks multiset adaptation).
subset_size_regime: All subsets (no cardinality restriction); internally Chan's algorithm considers Sigma_{<=k} for k up to 2^i on elements larger than t/2^i, and the witness in Le-Le uses at most m-1 copies. No Theta(n)-subset statement as such.
relevance_to_Nc: Indirect. Large |Sigma(X)| is exactly what these algorithms cannot handle; conversely small |OUT| forces many equal-sum pairs (pigeonhole: 2^n subsets into |OUT| values gives bins of average size 2^n/|OUT|), so the algorithms certify that the many-collision end is easy, matching the large-bin branch of C1. They do not bound N_c for inputs with moderate OUT. Chan's Obs 3.5 (sorted-block sums Sigma_i(X_1),...,Sigma_i(X_m) are disjoint, giving sum_j |Sigma_{<=k}(X_j)| <= O(k)|Sigma(X)|) is a reusable counting device for fixed size classes.
relevance_to_Dstar: Weak. D* counts distinct balanced half-sums of a solution support, which is a sub-structure; the output-sensitive algorithms bound running time by |OUT| for the whole input. Possible use: apply Chan/BFN to the restricted instance consisting of the support, which would solve in O~(D_support sqrt(|support|)) time if the support is known, but the support is the unknown.
applicability_gap: Parameters are polynomially bounded, whereas C1/C2 concern 2^{Theta(n)} distinct sums, Theta(n)-subsets and polynomial (not constant) doubling. Output-sensitive runtime O~(|OUT| sqrt n) is below 2^{n/2} only if |OUT| < 2^{n/2}/sqrt(n), so it covers part of the large-bin branch but not the intermediate-bin band; modular version gives O(m) only for explicit small modulus. Algorithms are DP/FFT-based and give no structural statement about equal-sum pairs.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Hard families for these algorithms: sets with 2^{Omega(n)} distinct subset sums, e.g. powers of 2 style/dissociated sets and random numbers of ~n bits (|OUT| ~ 2^n). The SETH reduction of ABHS produces dense-ish instances with t near 2^{n} / poly, showing the O(t) bound is tight up to 2^{o(n)} factors. For modular subset sum, Le-Le benchmarks use repeated generator (1, m-1) and powers of three as extreme inputs, not as C1/C2 hard instances.
dependency_chain: Composes with AKKN density dichotomy (large-bin branch), with Bringmann-Nakos/BFN output-sensitive algorithms (via Chan's derandomization) and with the Randolph-Wegrzycki structure work: dense end (these results) + small-doubling end (Randolph-Wegrzycki 2407.18228) + intermediate band left to C1/C2. Le-Le depends on DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar-Samal unit subset sums and Potepa's modular subset sum.
constructiveness: Fully constructive: Le-Le returns witnesses in O(m); Chan reports a witness per output in O~(1) per element after preprocessing (halver by method of conditional expectations is deterministic). Cost is polynomial in the parameter, i.e. exponential in n in the C1/C2 regime.
lean_formalizable: Not practical in a mathlib-free setting for the algorithms; the single combinatorial lemma worth formalizing is Chan's Observation 3.5 (disjointness of fixed-size sumsets over sorted blocks) and the pigeonhole link between |OUT| and bin size, both elementary.
computational_check: Le-Le tested with C++ on moduli up to 10^6 and validated against Boolean DP on 3,883 inputs; Chan has no experiments. For this repo, n<=40 is far outside the regime (|OUT| is ~2^n), but a script can compute |Sigma(X)| and bin-size histograms for n<=40 to see where a given instance lies relative to the 2^{n/2}/sqrt(n) output-sensitive threshold.
next_experiment: For the repo's hard-instance generators at n<=40, record |Sigma(X)| (distinct sums) versus 2^{n/2} and versus N_c and D*, to check whether the output-sensitive regime ever overlaps the region where D* <= 2^{0.311n}; this tests whether C2's forbidden region lies inside the already-easy |OUT| < 2^{n/2} region.
open_issues: Le-Le is a fresh unrefereed preprint (v2 of Sep 2026); correctness not independently verified by me beyond reading the proof outline. Chan states that Las Vegas conversion is open for the earlier randomized algorithms; log factors not optimized. Bringmann-Wellnitz and BFN were not read in primary text. [uncertain] BFN's exact bound O~(|OUT| sqrt(n)) and BW's t >> max*Sigma/n^2 threshold are taken from Chan's text and the BW abstract.
